archetype.name: Point Guard (Shanahan timing distributor)
archetype.definition: A rhythm passer who wins with quick, on-schedule throws over the middle and in the 10-19 yard window, spreading the ball to Evans, Kittle, McCaffrey and Samuel, with scrambles as a pressure valve rather than a centerpiece.

report.headline: Elite efficiency, soft schedule, and a clean-pocket run that can't last
report.take:
Purdy is what he has been since 2023: a timing passer in Kyle Shanahan's system who turns clean pockets and defined reads into chunk gains. His intended air yards (7.73) and aggressiveness (15%) are right in line with his last three seasons. The ball is not going deeper. It is being thrown on time to the right man, and that has produced a 0.527 EPA per dropback, second among 42 qualifiers.

Two things are driving it. The first is the middle of the field and the intermediate window. Throws between the numbers return 0.953 EPA on 81.5% completions, and the 10-19 yard range returns 0.671 EPA. Those are the dig-and-crosser concepts this offense is built on, and Mike Evans (1.034 EPA per target) has become the main beneficiary. The second is protection. He has been pressured on 10.6% of dropbacks, the lowest rate in the league, and the 49ers lead the NFL in fewest QB hits allowed. Under center, where play-action lives, his CPOE is +17.4, against -2.0 from shotgun. When he has been flushed, his 10 scrambles have produced 115 yards and 7 first downs.

The numbers hide two things: the schedule and some unrepeatable outcomes. Three of his four opponents (Miami, Arizona, Denver) now rank 23rd or worse in defensive EPA, and Weeks 2 and 3 produced most of his passing EPA (23.3 and 22.9). Against the one good defense, the Rams at No. 4, he threw at 4.6 intended air yards and posted a modest 4.8 EPA. Beyond the schedule, several numbers will not hold:
- Zero sacks on 122 dropbacks, from a passer whose pressure-to-sack rate has run 17-36% throughout his career.
- One interception, from a QB who has finished 51st-56th in interceptions three straight years.
- Seven red-zone touchdowns on 21 attempts.
- Two deep touchdowns on nine deep throws.

Where this heads: the skill is real. His 2023 and 2025 efficiency and his CPOE rank (5th in both seasons) back the short-and-intermediate dominance. Expect the sacks, interceptions and touchdown rate to drift toward his norms, though, starting with a Seattle defense that ranks third in EPA and fourth in hitting the quarterback. He should settle as a top-five efficiency passer rather than the near-record pace on the page now.

strengths.title: Middle-of-field timing game
strengths.body: Throws between the numbers and in the 10-19 yard band are the engine: crossers and digs off play-action, thrown on rhythm. This is scheme plus processing, and his career CPOE ranks of 5th in both 2023 and 2025 say it is durable, not a hot streak.

strengths.title: Play-action from under center
strengths.body: When he lines up under center his accuracy jumps far beyond expectation: a +17.4 CPOE and 0.643 EPA on 38 plays. That is the Shanahan bootleg and play-action menu working as designed. Repeated across seasons, this is a system edge rather than noise, though it depends on the run game and fullback looks that sell it.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay
strengths.body: He is not a designed runner, but his 10 scrambles have produced 115 yards and 7 first downs at nearly a point of EPA each. That is a meaningful bailout against defenses that collapse the pocket. His rushing has climbed from 13 yards as a rookie to 300-plus in 2024, so the escape element is part of his game now.

concerns.title: Turnover and sack luck will turn
concerns.body: One interception and zero sacks are well outside his history. He has ranked 51st-56th in interceptions each of the last three seasons, and his pressure-to-sack rate has never been below 16.7%. His bad-throw rate is genuinely improved, and the line is protecting him, but Week 3's 19.2% bad-throw game shows the loose throws are still in there. Expect both numbers to climb, especially against better fronts.

concerns.title: Inflated by a soft schedule
concerns.body: His two monster games came against Miami and Arizona, now 28th and 27th in defensive EPA. Against the 4th-ranked Rams he managed 4.8 passing EPA on mostly short throws. The touchdown rate (9.7%, first in the league) also leans on 7 red-zone scores in 21 attempts, which will not hold against defenses that tighten near the goal line.

concerns.title: Thin vertical game, weak designed runs
concerns.body: Only 9 of 112 attempts went 20+ yards, completed at 33%, so the deep shot is a complement, not a threat defenses must respect. Designed QB runs have been a loser: -0.366 EPA with a 28.6% stuff rate. Neither is fatal in this offense, but both limit his answers when the short game is taken away.

trend.note: His fantasy output has stayed in a 19.6-31.3 band every week. The efficiency, though, tracks the opponent: 4.8 and 8.5 passing EPA against the Rams and Broncos, over 22 against the Dolphins and Cardinals.

nextGame.headline: Best defense he's seen, but Seattle leaks underneath
nextGame.body:
Seattle's defense profiles as the hardest test of his season:
- Third in defensive EPA and second in success rate allowed.
- Second in allowing QB yardage (187.5 a game).
- Second in deep EPA allowed, so the shot plays should be quiet.

The opening is underneath. Seattle ranks 28th in EPA allowed on short throws, and his short-zone EPA (0.645 on 51 attempts) is where he lives. Seattle also ranks fourth in hit rate, so the clean pockets that have defined his season are the first thing under threat, and the zero-sack streak is unlikely to survive.

Availability cuts both ways. On his side, fullback Kyle Juszczyk (48% of snaps) is doubtful and reportedly out several weeks. That thins the heavy, under-center looks where Purdy has been most accurate and may push more of the game into shotgun, his weaker split. Christian Kirk remains on IR and has not played, so nothing changes there. On Seattle's side, DT Leonard Williams (70% of snaps) is questionable with an ankle, but his coach expects him to play, so assume the interior push is intact. The Seahawks are also without both Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. That further weakens an offense already 26th in rushing EPA, which could hand San Francisco shorter fields and a game state where Purdy doesn't have to chase.

keyMatchups.title: Short game versus soft underneath coverage
keyMatchups.body: Seattle takes away the deep ball but bleeds on short throws, ranking 28th there. His quick game is his best area, so expect volume on checkdowns, crossers and McCaffrey and Kittle targets rather than explosive shots.

keyMatchups.title: Seattle pressure versus clean-pocket streak
keyMatchups.body: The 49ers have allowed the fewest QB hits in the league, and Seattle is fourth in hitting quarterbacks. Who wins this decides whether Purdy keeps his rhythm or is forced into scrambles and the loose throws that have dogged his career interception totals.

keyMatchups.title: Juszczyk out, under-center game thinner
keyMatchups.body: His under-center splits (+17.4 CPOE) far outpace his shotgun work. Losing a fullback who plays half the snaps could reduce the heavy play-action looks that create those throws.

nextGame.watch: Whether he takes his first sack of the season early. If Seattle's front gets home, his efficiency drops toward his Week 1 level against the Rams; if not, the short game should carry him.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation will hold: accuracy over expectation, middle-of-field efficiency, and the No. 1 offense by EPA around him. Those have been true across 2023 and 2025. What regresses is everything that depended on nothing going wrong:
- Sacks: expect something like 4-6% of dropbacks.
- Interceptions: closer to his career rate of roughly one every other game.
- Touchdowns: a rate nearer 6-7% than 9.7%.

Efficiency per dropback should settle somewhere around 0.2-0.3, which is still a top-five range.

Volume is modest by design, since the 49ers pass only slightly more than situation predicts. His fantasy value rests on efficiency and touchdowns more than raw attempts, which makes him matchup-sensitive. Against top defenses like the Rams and Seahawks he looks more like a 200-230 yard passer; against the league's bottom third, the ceiling games return.
swingFactors: Pass protection holding up against better fronts
How much of the schedule is top-10 defenses
Health of the receiving corps (Evans, Kittle, McCaffrey)

bets.reason: Seattle allows the second-fewest QB yards (187.5 a game) and is second in deep EPA allowed. That caps his explosive plays, and his only game against a top-5 defense produced 205 yards. The soft underneath coverage keeps this from being a stronger play.

bets.market: Purdy passing TDs at his 2.75-a-game pace
bets.reason: That pace rests on 7 red-zone TDs in 21 attempts and a league-leading 9.7% TD rate built mostly against bottom-six defenses. Against the No. 3 defense by EPA, the season-long touchdown rate is the obvious read to bet against.

Seattle's defense ranks third in EPA, and its offense is run-heavy (25th in pass rate over expected), 26th in rushing EPA, and missing both Charbonnet and Price. San Francisco's one game against an elite defense, at the Rams, finished 27-7, far under its total.

The 49ers have the league's No. 1 offense by EPA and have covered three of four. Seattle's offense ranks only 12th and is down its top two backs, so getting points in a game this even looks slightly favorable.

confidence.note: Four games and 113 attempts, three against bottom-six defenses. Career efficiency supports the core profile but not the sack, interception and TD rates.
